title.narrative: NAMA - Solar district heating

description.narrative: Mongolia relies on coal for more than 90% of their electricity and heating needs, resulting in per-capita GHG emissions 2.7 times the global average. In urban areas heat services are provided through district heating networks fueled by coal power, thus finding low carbon alternatives to meet heating needs is a key challenge to reduce GHG emissions and transition to a green economy in Mongolia where more than 50% of GHG emissions come from the energy sector.Solar district heating is one of the promising technologies to increase the proportion of renewable energy in district heating and pave the way for longer term energy transition. In Europe more than 300 solar district heating plants are operating and given Mongolia is rich in solar energy resources, solar district heating could help to break the country's reliance on coal and demonstrate viable alternatives to meet the country's heating needs.The Nama Facility's Ambition initiative emphasizes innovation and introduced the possibility to support to pilot projects for novel technologies before moving into a larger scale project. Thus, the Mongolia team would like to propose a pilot project for solar district heating in Dalanzadgad, Umnugobi Province to the NAMA Facility Ambition Initiative Round 2.
